editorial:
Imagine driving down a lonely highway and crossing paths with a preaching redneck who has a very dark secret. That is exactly what happens in this wild ride. You meet Jake, a crazy guy who thinks he is doing God's work while he actually kidnaps strangers to harvest their organs. He sells these parts to a shady guy named Mr. Stone to make a quick buck. The movie has a gritty, low-budget feel that makes the whole thing feel like a weird dream. It balances gross-out horror with some really dark jokes, making it a trip that is both scary and funny at the same time.

What really makes this work is the character of April. She is handicapped, and Jake thinks she will be an easy target, but she turns out to be way tougher than he ever expected. The pacing is quick, and the acting feels natural for this kind of b-movie. While some of the effects look old, they actually add to the charm. If you love campy horror, you should grab the 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection to see all the gore in detail, or just rent it on Apple TV for a movie night with friends.
endingExplained: In the final showdown, April uses her intelligence and surroundings to outsmart Jake. She manages to fight back during a chaotic struggle, eventually turning Jake's own medical tools against him. She kills Jake in a messy way and escapes the house just as the police arrive. Mr. Stone tries to cover his tracks, but April provides the evidence needed to bring down the whole organ-selling ring, finally getting her freedom and justice.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves 80s and 90s sleazy horror movies.
